newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds mixed, focus turns to EMU convergence.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds mixed, focus turns to EMU convergence.

text.p: Irish bonds experienced mixed fortunes in active late trade on Wednesday as focus switched away from the currency markets to the issues of convergence and international bond market conditions, dealers said.

"The Irish market on the day was incredibly patchy across the curve with massive yield curve swings being the highlight. All markets have been very volatile but we are closing at reasonably good levels," a dealer said.
"Generally, conditions are quite supportive. The exception is the Irish short-end which has been a bit offered. Very unusual price action on the day in Ireland," he added.

By 1630 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000 had eased 30p from Tuesday's close to 105.85 to yield 6.18 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had risen 55p from the close to 108.10 to yield 6.71 percent.
Dealers said the market would keep a close eye on the end-September banking statistics due for release from the Irish Central Bank at 1630 GMT on Thursday.
"Domestic credit figures are hanging over the short-end of the market a bit," the dealer said.
